Source: https://github.com/Liceron/nexura/blob/main/docs/a2a.md

# Agent2Agent (A2A) interoperability

[A2A](https://a2a-protocol.org) is an open protocol that lets agents built with different frameworks talk to each other. Nexura speaks it in both directions: `A2AServer` serves a Nexura agent or team as an A2A agent, and `A2AClient` / `remote_agent_tool` call any remote A2A agent from a Nexura agent.

**Protocol version implemented: A2A 1.0, JSON-RPC binding** (methods `SendMessage`, `SendStreamingMessage`, `GetTask`, `CancelTask`; agent card at `/.well-known/agent-card.json`). The 0.3 method names `message/send`, `message/stream`, `tasks/get` and `tasks/cancel` are also accepted, answered in the 0.3 payload shape. Field names, error codes and states were checked against the official `a2a-sdk` sources, and the offline tests in `experiments/interop` run Nexura against `a2a-sdk` 1.2.3 in both directions (see [Verified against the reference SDK](#verified-against-the-reference-sdk)); that package is not a dependency of Nexura.

## Try it in-process

This example serves an agent and calls it through an `httpx.ASGITransport`, so no port is opened. Against a real deployment you only change the URL.

```python
import asyncio

import httpx

from nexura_agents import A2AClient, A2AServer, Agent, FakeModel

support = Agent(
    name="Support",
    description="Answers questions about orders.",
    instructions="Help customers.",
    model=FakeModel(responses=["Order A1 is shipped.", "Yes, still shipped."]),
)

server = A2AServer(support, url="http://support.test/")
app = server.http_app(token="s3cret")


async def main() -> None:
    client = A2AClient(
        "http://support.test",
        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer s3cret"},
        transport=httpx.ASGITransport(app=app),
    )
    card = await client.get_card()
    assert card["name"] == "Support"

    task = await client.send("Where is order A1?")
    assert task.state == "completed" and task.text == "Order A1 is shipped."

    # Follow-ups in the same context continue the conversation.
    again = await client.send("Still shipped?", context_id=task.context_id)
    assert again.text == "Yes, still shipped."

    # Streaming yields the task, status changes and the output artifact.
    kinds = [event.kind async for event in client.stream("one more", context_id=task.context_id)]
    assert kinds[0] == "task" and kinds[-1] == "status"


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Serve with uvicorn

```python notest
# app.py
from nexura_agents import A2AServer, Agent

agent = Agent(
    name="Support",
    description="Answers order questions.",
    instructions="...",
    model="openai:gpt-4o-mini",
)
server = A2AServer(agent, url="https://agents.example.com/")
app = server.http_app(token="a-long-random-token", allowed_origins=[])
```

Run it with `uvicorn app:app` and point any A2A client at `https://agents.example.com`. `url` is the public address of the JSON-RPC endpoint (the app answers `POST /`; pass `path=` to `http_app` to move it), and it is what the agent card advertises.

`A2AServer(agent_or_team, *, name=None, description=None, url, version="1.0.0", skills=None, deps=None, runner=None, signing_key=None, signing_kid=None, signing_jku=None)`

- A `Team` (`SequentialAgent`, `ParallelAgent`, `LoopAgent`) is served as one agent.
- `skills` are card skills as dicts (`id`, `name`, `description`, `tags`); by default one skill describes the agent.
- `deps` and `runner` work as in [`AgentMCPServer`](serving-over-mcp.md): pass a `Runner` to apply usage limits, hooks or budgets.
- `signing_key` / `signing_kid` / `signing_jku`: sign the served card (see [Signed agent cards](#signed-agent-cards)).

`http_app(*, token=None, allowed_origins=(), max_body_bytes=4 MiB, max_tasks=1000, task_ttl_seconds=3600, path="/")`

- The card is public and never contains secrets. When a `token` is set, the card advertises bearer authentication and every JSON-RPC call needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (compared in constant time).
- Requests with an `Origin` header are refused (403) unless listed in `allowed_origins`.
- Bodies over `max_body_bytes` get 413. Errors never include internal details.
- At most `max_tasks` tasks and conversation contexts are kept, least recently used first, and idle ones expire after `task_ttl_seconds`. Running tasks are never evicted; when every slot is running, new requests get an error until one finishes. The store is in memory: tasks are lost on restart.
- Task ids are random (144 bits). One token guards the whole server, so every holder can read, continue and cancel every task. Run one server per tenant if you need isolation.
- Outputs: text output is a text part; an agent with `output_type` (or a team returning a model, dict or list) is a data part. Text and data parts of a message become the prompt; file parts with inline bytes or a URL become attachments (inline bytes are not kept in task history).
- A dropped stream does not cancel the run; use `CancelTask`.

## Call a remote A2A agent as a tool

```python
import asyncio

import httpx

from nexura_agents import A2AClient, A2AServer, Agent, FakeModel, ToolCall, remote_agent_tool

remote = Agent(
    name="Support",
    description="Answers questions about orders.",
    instructions="Help.",
    model=FakeModel(responses=["Order A1 is shipped."]),
)
transport = httpx.ASGITransport(app=A2AServer(remote, url="http://support.test/").http_app())


async def main() -> None:
    client = A2AClient("http://support.test", transport=transport)
    await client.get_card()  # lets the tool description come from the card's skills
    support_tool = remote_agent_tool(client)

    concierge = Agent(
        name="Concierge",
        instructions="Delegate order questions.",
        model=FakeModel(
            responses=[
                [ToolCall(id="1", name=support_tool.name, arguments={"request": "Where is A1?"})],
                "It is shipped.",
            ]
        ),
        tools=[support_tool],
    )
    result = await concierge.run_async("Where is order A1?")
    assert result.output == "It is shipped."


asyncio.run(main())
```

```python notest
agent = Agent(
    name="Concierge",
    instructions="...",
    model="openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    tools=[
        remote_agent_tool(
            "https://partner.example.com/agent",
            headers={"Authorization": "Bearer ..."},
            description="Partner agent that checks stock levels.",
        )
    ],
)
```

`A2AClient(url, *, headers=None, timeout=60, transport=None, policy=None, card_keys=None, card_algorithms=None)` offers `get_card()`, `send(text_or_parts, *, task_id=None, context_id=None)`, `stream(...)`, `get_task(id)`, `cancel(id)` and `decide(task_id, approve=..., reject=...)`. It returns `A2ATask` (`state`, `text`, `data`, `output`, `pending_approvals`, `raw`). It uses the 1.0 interface from the card and falls back to the 0.3 shapes for older cards.

`remote_agent_tool(url_or_client, *, name=None, description=None, requires_approval=False)` returns a `Tool` with one `request` string. It returns the remote output (structured output stays a dict). If the remote task is `input-required` or fails, the tool raises a `ToolError` the calling model sees, like `Agent.as_tool`; approvals cannot be given inside a tool call. Set `requires_approval=True` to make your own run pause before calling a partner agent.

Outbound safety matches `MCPServer.http`: requests go through the SSRF-safe client and `DestinationPolicy`; the default policy permits loopback and private addresses for the host you configured, cloud metadata addresses are always blocked, and redirects are not followed. A card that advertises an endpoint on a different host is refused unless you list that host in `DestinationPolicy(allowed_hosts=[...])`. Pass a stricter `policy=` for untrusted URLs.

## Approvals over A2A

A run that reaches a tool with `requires_approval` pauses. The task becomes `input-required`; its status message lists the pending calls with their digests, as text and as a data part `{"pendingApprovals": [{"key", "tool", "arguments", "digest"}]}`. The client continues the same task by sending a message with that `taskId` and a data part `{"approve": [...keys] | true | {key: digest}, "reject": {key: reason}}`. Every pending call needs exactly one decision. The server resumes from the stored `RunInterruption`, so approval is bound to the exact arguments it showed; an `approve` mapping whose digest does not match is refused with `-32602` and the task stays open. Team keys look like `path:call_id`.

```python
import asyncio

import httpx

from nexura_agents import A2AClient, A2AServer, Agent, FakeModel, ToolCall, tool

refunds_sent: list[str] = []


@tool(requires_approval=True)
def refund(order_id: str) -> str:
    """Refund an order."""
    refunds_sent.append(order_id)
    return f"refunded {order_id}"


agent = Agent(
    name="Refunds",
    instructions="Refund orders.",
    model=FakeModel(
        responses=[[ToolCall(id="r1", name="refund", arguments={"order_id": "A1"})], "Refunded."]
    ),
    tools=[refund],
)
app = A2AServer(agent, url="http://refunds.test/").http_app()


async def main() -> None:
    client = A2AClient("http://refunds.test", transport=httpx.ASGITransport(app=app))
    task = await client.send("Refund order A1")
    assert task.is_input_required and refunds_sent == []
    call = task.pending_approvals[0]
    print("needs approval:", call["tool"], call["arguments"])

    done = await client.decide(task.id, approve={call["key"]: call["digest"]})
    assert done.state == "completed" and refunds_sent == ["A1"]


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Signed agent cards

A2A 1.0 lets a provider sign its agent card with a JSON Web Signature over the RFC 8785
canonical form of the card (empty strings, lists and objects removed, `signatures`
excluded). Nexura signs and verifies such cards. Signing needs the `cryptography`
package, which `nexura-runtime` installs; with `nexura-agents` alone, install
`nexura-agents[signing]`.

```python
import asyncio

import httpx
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import ec

from nexura_agents import A2AClient, A2AServer, Agent, FakeModel
from nexura_agents.a2a import AgentCardSignatureError

key = ec.generate_private_key(ec.SECP256R1())  # in production: load your private key
agent = Agent(name="Support", instructions="", model=FakeModel(responses=["Shipped."]))
server = A2AServer(agent, url="http://support.test/", signing_key=key, signing_kid="2026-10")
transport = httpx.ASGITransport(app=server.http_app())


async def main() -> None:
    trusted = {"2026-10": key.public_key()}
    client = A2AClient("http://support.test", transport=transport, card_keys=trusted)
    assert (await client.send("Where is A1?")).text == "Shipped."
    assert client.card_verified_kid == "2026-10"

    impostor = ec.generate_private_key(ec.SECP256R1()).public_key()
    wary = A2AClient("http://support.test", transport=transport, card_keys={"2026-10": impostor})
    try:
        await wary.send("Where is A1?")
    except AgentCardSignatureError:
        pass  # nothing was sent: the card did not verify
    else:
        raise AssertionError("expected the card to be refused")


asyncio.run(main())
```

- **Serving:** `A2AServer(signing_key=..., signing_kid=...)` adds one entry to the card's
  `signatures` (`alg` chosen from the key: ES256, ES384, EdDSA or RS256; `typ` "JOSE";
  optional `jku`). The signature covers the card as served, including the bearer
  `securitySchemes` that `http_app(token=...)` adds.
- **Calling:** with `card_keys={kid: public_key_or_jwk}` the client requires a signature
  that verifies with one of those keys before it uses the card; otherwise every call
  raises `AgentCardSignatureError` and the card is not cached. Accepted algorithms
  default to ES256, ES384, RS256, PS256 and EdDSA (`card_algorithms=` narrows them).
  Signatures with unknown `kid`s or `crit` headers are skipped, so a rotated key can sit
  next to the current one.
- **Without `card_keys`** signatures are not checked at all, and an unsigned card is
  accepted. Keys are never fetched from a card's `jku` URL: trust comes only from the keys
  you configure. `sign_agent_card` and `verify_agent_card` (in `nexura_agents.a2a`) work
  on plain card dicts if you manage cards yourself.

## Verified against the reference SDK

`experiments/interop` is a separate uv project (its own `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`)
that installs the official `a2a-sdk` 1.2.3 next to Nexura and runs offline on 127.0.0.1:

- the `a2a-sdk` card resolver parses Nexura's card and verifies its signature with the
  SDK's own verifier (and rejects it with the wrong key);
- the `a2a-sdk` 1.0 client sends to Nexura (non-streaming and streaming) and reads the
  task back with `GetTask`; the SDK's v0.3 compatibility transport also works against
  Nexura's 0.3 method names;
- Nexura's client verifies a card signed by the SDK's `create_agent_card_signer`, refuses
  it with an untrusted key or after tampering, sends and streams to an `a2a-sdk` server,
  and uses the 0.3 wire against the SDK's v0.3 compatibility endpoint.

Other A2A implementations (other languages, hosted agents) have not been tested.

## What is and is not implemented

Implemented: agent card with `supportedInterfaces`, signed agent cards (sign and verify), `SendMessage`, `SendStreamingMessage` (server-sent events), `GetTask`, `CancelTask`, text, data and file parts, task states `submitted`, `working`, `completed`, `failed`, `canceled` and `input-required`, contexts, the A2A and JSON-RPC error codes, the `A2A-Version` header (1.0 and 0.3 accepted), and the 0.3 method names.

Not implemented: push notifications (`-32003`), `ListTasks`, `SubscribeToTask` and the authenticated extended card (answered with their specific error codes), the HTTP+JSON and gRPC bindings, fetching signing keys from `jku`, OAuth and other security schemes beyond a static bearer token, extensions, multi-tenancy, task persistence, and the 0.3 agent card format on the server side (the client does read 0.3 cards). Interoperability is verified against the official `a2a-sdk` 1.2.3 only (above), not against other third-party agents.

## Talk to other agents with A2A

`A2AServer(agent_or_team, url=...).http_app(token=...)` serves an agent card and the
Agent2Agent 1.0 JSON-RPC methods (`SendMessage`, `SendStreamingMessage`, `GetTask`,
`CancelTask`; 0.3 method names accepted). Approvals appear as `input-required` and are
continued with digest-bound decisions. `A2AClient` and `remote_agent_tool(url)` let your
agent call any A2A agent. Agent cards can be signed (`signing_key=`) and verified
(`card_keys=`). Not implemented: push notifications, ListTasks and Subscribe, the HTTP+JSON
and gRPC bindings, and OAuth. Tested offline against the official `a2a-sdk` 1.2.3 in both
directions; not against other third-party agents. See `docs/a2a.md`.

---

Source: https://github.com/Liceron/nexura/blob/main/docs/langflow-import.md

# Importing Langflow flows (Nexura V2)

`nexura_runtime.integrations.langflow` reads flows saved by Nexura V2 (Langflow 1.12.x JSON)
and runs them on the Nexura SDK. The
importer never executes the component code stored in the flow, never reads API keys from it
and makes no network call unless a tool you allowed does.

The importer, the runner and the export back to Langflow JSON are open source. The V2-shaped
run API (`V2FlowServer`), the V2 SSE event shapes, V2 identity and policy adapters and the
shadow-run migration harness are part of the closed edition.

```text
load(flow)  ->  ImportedFlow (+ ImportReport)  ->  build(imported, models=...)  ->  BuiltFlow
                                                      run_async / run / stream_events(mapper=...)
```

## Offline example

```python
import asyncio
import json

from nexura_agents import FakeModel
from nexura_runtime.integrations.langflow import build, load, run_flow


def node(nid, cls, template=None):
    return {
        "id": nid,
        "type": "genericNode",
        "data": {"id": nid, "type": cls, "node": {"display_name": cls, "template": template or {}}},
    }


def edge(src, out, dst, field):
    return {
        "source": src,
        "target": dst,
        "data": {
            "sourceHandle": {"id": src, "name": out},
            "targetHandle": {"id": dst, "fieldName": field},
        },
    }


agent_template = {
    "model": {"type": "model", "value": [{"name": "gpt-4o-mini", "provider": "OpenAI"}]},
    "system_prompt": {"type": "str", "value": "You are a concise assistant."},
}
flow = {
    "name": "demo",
    "data": {
        "nodes": [
            node("ChatInput-1", "ChatInput"),
            node("Agent-1", "Agent", agent_template),
            node("ChatOutput-1", "ChatOutput"),
        ],
        "edges": [
            edge("ChatInput-1", "message", "Agent-1", "input_value"),
            edge("Agent-1", "response", "ChatOutput-1", "input_value"),
        ],
    },
}

imported = load(flow)  # raises on bad JSON, bad handles, cycles, unsupported nodes
print([n.class_name for n in imported.report.supported])

# Offline: every model step uses a local fake. In production pass a model, a
# mapping or a factory (see "Models and keys").
model = FakeModel(["Hello from the imported flow"])
print(run_flow(imported, "hi", models=model))

built = build(imported, models=FakeModel(["built answer"]))


async def main():
    result = await built.run_async("hi", session_id="demo")
    print(result.output, json.dumps(result.outputs)[:60])


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Supported components

| Langflow class | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| `ChatInput`, `ChatOutput` | run input (with its session id) and result text |
| `TextInput` | constant text |
| `Prompt` | `{variable}` template; each variable is filled by the edge wired to it, else the template value |
| `ParserComponent`, `parser` | pattern with `{text}` applied to its input (`mode` Stringify passes text through) |
| `LanguageModelComponent` | one plain model call (no tools, no history); its `model_output` can also configure an Agent or StructuredOutput |
| `Agent` | SDK `Agent`: system prompt, model, tools, `n_messages` as history window, `max_iterations` as `max_turns`, `output_schema` rows as structured output |
| `StructuredOutput` | an agent with `output_type` built from the schema table; outputs the JSON as text |
| `CalculatorComponent` | safe arithmetic tool (no names, calls or huge exponents) |
| `URLComponent` | fetch tool using the SDK `web_fetch_tool` (private addresses blocked); domains in the flow's `urls` field are the only ones allowed; with no domains the tool refuses every fetch (`error: refused`) |
| `UnifiedWebSearch` | search tool backed by `search_provider=`; without one it returns a `web_search_not_configured` error |
| note nodes | skipped, listed in the report |

Everything else (File, Memory, Knowledge, SQL, SaveToFile, Loop, BatchRun, hidden bundles,
unknown or custom components, nodes without `data.type`) is reported as unsupported with a
reason unless you load with `extended=True` (next section). A node whose `code` does not match
its recorded `metadata.code_hash` is unsupported (edited component); code with no hash to check
is ignored with a warning.

## Extended components (V3)

`load(flow, extended=True)` also recognises File, MemoryBase, KnowledgeBase/Knowledge,
LoopComponent, SQLComponent and SplitText. They are opt-in so existing callers see no change.
The caller supplies the resources through `build(imported, v3=V3Options(...))`; a flow never
names a path root, a database or an API key itself. Component source code is never run.

| Class | Fields used | Outputs | Becomes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `File` | `path` or `file_path` (string or list; may be wired) | `message`, `data`, `dataframe`, `raw_content` (all the text) | Reads text files and PDFs under `V3Options.files_root` |
| `MemoryBase` | `search_query`, `n_messages` (match limit, 1-50) | `component_as_tool` (tool `search_memory`), `messages`, `message` | Searches the run's saved session history in the SDK session store |
| `KnowledgeBase`, `Knowledge` | `knowledge_base` (or `knowledge_base_name`, `kb_name`), `top_k`, `search_query` | `component_as_tool` (tool `search_knowledge`), `results`, `dataframe`, `message` | Embeds the query and searches the SDK vector store (`results` is the passage text) |
| `LoopComponent` | `data` (wired or literal) | `item`, `done` | A bounded map: the body runs once per item |
| `SQLComponent` | `query` (a literal fixes the statement), `database_url` (never used) | `component_as_tool` (tool `sql_query`), `run_sql_query`, `message` | One parameterised statement on the connection `V3Options.sql_connection` |
| `SplitText` | `data_inputs`, `chunk_size` (1000), `chunk_overlap` (200), `separator` (newline) | `chunks` and `dataframe` (JSON list), `message` | Character chunker; its `chunks` feed a Loop |

Not used from these classes: any other visible field with a non-empty value is listed in the
report as `option '<name>' is not supported and was ignored`. Secrets never come from a flow:
a literal `database_url` or API key is blanked, and a `load_from_db` reference to a
`database_url` is ignored with a warning (it is not a required variable). `KnowledgeIngestion`,
`SaveToFile`, `BatchRunComponent`, `ArXivComponent`, `AstraDB` and audio components stay
unsupported.

**File.** `files_root` is required. A path with `..` is refused, an absolute path must resolve
(after symlinks) inside the root, and only `.txt .md .markdown .csv .tsv .json .yaml .log` and
`.pdf` are read. A file over `max_file_bytes` (1 MB) is refused before it is read, binary
content is refused, and PDF text goes through the platform's PDF parser (`pypdf`, at most
`max_pdf_pages`). A refusal raises `ComponentRefusedError`.

**Memory.** The tool reads only the history of the current `session_id` (it needs a session
store); another session, or a run with no session, finds nothing. A `session_id` set on the
node is ignored.

**Knowledge.** Needs `V3Options.embedder` (`embed(text) -> list[float]`, sync or async) and uses
`V3Options.vector_store` (default: a fresh `InMemoryVectorStore`). Every search is scoped to
`workspace_id`. With `knowledge_scope="session"` the collection also depends on the run's
session, so one session never reads another's passages. The knowledge base name is limited to
letters, digits and `_ . -`. `ingest_knowledge(opts, name, texts, session_id=...)` fills it.

**Loop.** Items come from a list, a JSON list in text, or one item per non-empty line. The
nodes between `item` and the feedback edge (the edge into the Loop's `item` handle) are the
body. Each item runs the body once with no session history, so items never see each other, and
the feedback edge's value is collected. `done` is those values joined by newlines (the list is
also in `node_outputs[loop]["items"]`). More than `max_loop_items` (100) items raises
`ComponentRefusedError`; items are never truncated. A body vertex is reported once with its
last iteration's values. Nested loops, a loop with `item` consumers but no feedback edge, and
overlapping bodies are build errors.

**SQL.** Read-only by default: the statement must be one SELECT, WITH or VALUES, and the
database connection runs with `query_only`. `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE` and `REPLACE` need
`sql_allow_write=True` and a connection registered with `read_only=False`; DDL, `ATTACH`,
`PRAGMA`, `VACUUM` and extension loading are always refused, and so is any second statement.
Values go through bound parameters (`?` or `:name`), never into the text. Rows are capped by
`sql_max_rows` and `sql_max_bytes`. A tool refusal is returned to the model as `{"error":
"refused"}`. Connections come from `SqlConnectionManager`; the flow's `database_url` is never a
DSN.

```python
import asyncio
import json
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from nexura_agents import FakeModel
from nexura_runtime.integrations.langflow import V3Options, build, load


def node(nid, cls, template=None):
    return {
        "id": nid,
        "type": "genericNode",
        "data": {"id": nid, "type": cls, "node": {"display_name": cls, "template": template or {}}},
    }


def edge(src, out, dst, field):
    return {
        "source": src,
        "target": dst,
        "data": {
            "sourceHandle": {"id": src, "name": out},
            "targetHandle": {"id": dst, "fieldName": field},
        },
    }


def field(value):
    return {"type": "str", "value": value}


root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
(root / "todo.txt").write_text("write docs\nship it", encoding="utf-8")

flow = {
    "name": "file-loop",
    "data": {
        "nodes": [
            node("File-1", "File", {"path": field("todo.txt")}),
            node("Loop-1", "LoopComponent"),
            node("Prompt-1", "Prompt", {"template": field("TODO: {item}"), "item": field("")}),
            node("ChatOutput-1", "ChatOutput"),
        ],
        "edges": [
            edge("File-1", "message", "Loop-1", "data"),
            edge("Loop-1", "item", "Prompt-1", "item"),
            edge("Prompt-1", "prompt", "Loop-1", "item"),  # feedback into the Loop
            edge("Loop-1", "done", "ChatOutput-1", "input_value"),
        ],
    },
}
imported = load(flow, extended=True)
built = build(imported, v3=V3Options(files_root=root, max_loop_items=10))
print(asyncio.run(built.run_async("go")).output)
```

## Agent-to-agent semantics

Langflow is a dataflow graph, so an Agent `response` wired into another Agent's `input_value`
is a **pipeline step**: the first agent finishes, then its text is the second agent's input
(like `SequentialAgent`). Handoffs are not used, because Langflow has no model-driven
transfer of control. An Agent wired into another Agent's `tools` port becomes an
**agent-as-tool** (`Agent.as_tool`). Nodes run in dependency order, one at a time.

## The import report

`imported.report` holds `supported`, `unsupported` (class, id, reason, whether it is on the
path to a ChatOutput), `notes`, `warnings`, `unsupported_edges` and `required_variables`.
By default an unsupported node on the path to a ChatOutput raises `UnsupportedFlowError`
(its `.report` has the details). `load(flow, strict=False)` keeps the report instead and
`build` runs what it can; dropped nodes and edges appear in `built.warnings`.
Malformed input raises `FlowFormatError` with every problem listed; limits (5 MiB, 1000
nodes, 5000 edges by default) raise `FlowTooLargeError`. Both handle forms are accepted: the
parsed `data.sourceHandle`/`data.targetHandle` objects are preferred, then the string with
its U+0153 quote escapes. A cycle that does not pass through a Loop is rejected.

## Models and keys

`models=` accepts `None` (a provider table: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama, Sarvam,
Vertex), one model or spec string for every step, a mapping keyed by node id, display name,
`"provider:name"` or `"*"`, or a factory `fn(ModelRef) -> model`. Unknown providers raise
`ModelMappingError`. Keys are never read from the flow: fields with `load_from_db` name a
variable, and you supply it with `variables={"OPENAI_API_KEY": "..."}`. Missing variables are
all listed in one `MissingVariablesError`. A key variable is required only when the provider
table builds the model; a factory receives it in `ModelRef.api_key` when you supplied it.

## Tweaks

`build(imported, tweaks={"Agent-1": {"system_prompt": "..."}, "Prompt": {...}})` overrides
fields by node id, or by display name when unique. A non-dict value is a global override for
every node that has that field. A literal value replaces a `load_from_db` reference. Refused
(all reported together in `TweakRefusedError.refused`): `code`, database/query fields
(`database_url`, `query`, `sql`, ...), secret fields (use `variables=`), unknown nodes or
fields, ambiguous display names.

## Tools and network

`tools={"CalculatorComponent": my_tool}` replaces a tool node by node id, display name,
class name or kind. `http_transport=httpx.MockTransport(...)` serves URL tools offline and
`search_provider=fn(query)` supplies web search results. Tests should always use these.

## Running

- `run_flow(imported_or_built, "text", session_id=..., session_store=..., **build_kwargs)`
  returns the ChatOutput text (`run_flow_async` for async code).
- `built.run_async(...)` returns a `FlowRunResult` (`output`, `outputs`, `node_outputs`,
  per-node SDK `run_results`). `output_component=` picks one ChatOutput by id or name.
- Sessions: pass `session_id` (plus a `session_store`, or a built-in in-memory store is
  used). Each Agent keeps its own history keyed by the JSON-encoded triple
  `[session_id, context_id, node id]`, so ids containing `:` cannot collide. An Agent's
  literal `context_id` narrows the key and never replaces the caller's session id: distinct
  sessions never share history, even when the flow sets the same `context_id`.
- Streaming: `built.stream_events(..., mapper=...)` and `stream_flow_events(..., mapper=...)`
  yield the events your `FlowEventMapper` builds for each step of the run (`vertices_sorted`,
  `build_start`, `add_message`, `token`, `end_vertex`, `build_end`, `end`, `error`), while a
  node runs, not after it ends. `mapper=` is required: the open-source edition ships no event
  wire format of its own.
- Prompt templates: `{{`/`}}` are un-escaped in the template text only; substituted values
  are inserted verbatim.
- Loops: cycles through a Loop component are tolerated (reported unsupported); any other
  cycle raises `FlowFormatError`. Non-JSON strings that are not an existing file raise
  `FlowFormatError`.

## Exporting back to Langflow

`export_flow(imported, original=...)` writes an `ImportedFlow` back to Langflow 1.12.x JSON so
V2's editor can keep opening it during the transition.

```python
from nexura_runtime.integrations.langflow import export_flow, load


def node(nid, cls, template):
    return {
        "id": nid,
        "type": "genericNode",
        "position": {"x": 10, "y": 20},
        "data": {"id": nid, "type": cls, "node": {"display_name": cls, "template": template}},
    }


original = {
    "name": "demo",
    "data": {
        "nodes": [
            node("TextInput-a", "TextInput", {"input_value": {"type": "str", "value": "hi"}}),
            node("ChatOutput-b", "ChatOutput", {"input_value": {"type": "str", "value": ""}}),
        ],
        "edges": [],
        "viewport": {"x": 0, "y": 0, "zoom": 1},
    },
}
flow = load(original, strict=False)
assert export_flow(flow, original=original) == original  # no edits: identical
flow.nodes["TextInput-a"].fields["input_value"] = "hello"
edited = export_flow(flow, original=original)
assert edited["data"]["nodes"][0]["data"]["node"]["template"]["input_value"]["value"] == "hello"
assert edited["data"]["nodes"][0]["position"] == {"x": 10, "y": 20}
```

How it works: the export starts from a deep copy of `original` and applies only the
difference between your `ImportedFlow` and a fresh `load(original)`. Everything the SDK does not
model (component `code`, `code_hash`, positions, `measured`, viewport, outputs, `selected_output`,
notes, unsupported nodes and their edges, edge ids and handle text) is carried over unchanged.

What can change in the output:

- Template `value` (and `load_from_db`) of fields you edited in `flow.nodes[id].fields`.
- `display_name` of a node, and the top-level `name`/`description` when present in the original.
- Edges you removed from `flow.edges` disappear; nodes you deleted from `flow.nodes` disappear
  with their edges. Edges you added are written with both handle encodings (the parsed
  `data.sourceHandle`/`data.targetHandle` objects and the oe-ligature strings, keys sorted), and
  the output name and target field must exist in the original node's `outputs`/`template`.
- Every exported node, including unsupported pass-through nodes, has its literal secrets
  blanked, never carried over, whether or not `load()` was called with `extended=True`. A field
  is secret when its template entry has `password: true` or `_input_type: SecretStrInput`, when
  its name is `api_key`, `apikey`, `token`, `secret`, `password` or `access_token`
  (case-insensitive), or when it is a connection field (`database_url`, `connection_string`).
  This is why the `f7_tweaks` fixture, which holds a literal `database_url`, round-trips with
  that one value emptied. Variable references (`load_from_db` plus the variable name) are kept.
- An unchanged field is detected type-exactly: `False` vs `0`, `True` vs `1`, `1` vs `1.0` and
  `"1"` vs `1` are all edits.

Refusals (`FlowExportError`, a `LangflowImportError`):

- editing or adding an unsupported node, or wiring an edge to one (unchanged ones pass through);
- writing a literal value into a secret field (use a global variable reference instead);
- an edge whose output or target field is not in the node, or whose endpoint is missing;
- an added edge into a target field with empty `input_types`, or whose source output types
  include none of the target's `input_types` (edges to or from SDK-only nodes, which carry no
  type metadata, are not type-checked);
- deleting a field from `flow.nodes[id].fields` (Langflow components cannot lose template
  fields);
- changing a node's component class, or adding a template field that does not exist;
- a node with no original (SDK-only) unless you pass `allow_sdk_only=True`.

Missing `code`: the SDK never invents component source. Langflow builds a vertex from
`template.code.value` (V2's lfx reads it in graph/vertex param handling and flow validation, and
only the editor's component-update step fills it from the registry), so a node without `code`
may fail to build until the editor updates it. That is why SDK-only nodes are refused by
default. With `allow_sdk_only=True` they are emitted without a `code` field and marked
`metadata.nexura_sdk_only`; this path is unverified against a live Langflow. Without `original`
every node is SDK-only, so `export_flow(flow)` needs the same flag.

## Limits

Not live-tested against real models or against real V2-saved flows. Hand-written fixtures
follow the documented format. One flow run is sequential. The extended components are opt-in
(`extended=True`). File, SQL and Knowledge nodes build only when a `V3Options` is supplied;
without one they refuse to build. Memory, Loop and SplitText always work.

Extended-component caps: SQL results are capped by `sql_max_bytes` while rows are fetched
(SQLite is told to refuse any value over the cap, so a huge blob is never built); a File node's
`max_file_bytes` applies to the sum of all its paths and `max_file_paths` (default 20) caps the
path count; saved history is keyed by a content hash of the flow, so two flows sharing a store
and session id never see each other's messages (this includes the Memory tool). Coverage
numbers count classes, not instances: an instance may set options that are ignored with a
load warning.

---

Source: https://github.com/Liceron/nexura/blob/main/docs/providers.md

# Models and providers

An agent talks to a model through a provider. You can pass a model object, or a string of the form `"provider:model"` and let Nexura build the provider for you. This page covers the providers that ship with `nexura-agents` (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Sarvam) and Vertex AI (the separate `nexura-vertex` package), how credentials are found, how reasoning tokens show up in usage, and how to retry and fail over between models. Everything except the live-call examples runs offline.

## Start offline

`FakeModel` needs no key and makes no network call. The string `"test"` builds a `FakeModel` that answers every turn with the same fixed text.

```python
from nexura_agents import Agent, FakeModel

agent = Agent(name="Demo", instructions="Be brief.", model=FakeModel(responses=["Hello!"]))
assert agent.run("Hi").final_output == "Hello!"

# "test" is a shortcut for an offline model with a fixed reply.
quick = Agent(name="Quick", instructions="Be brief.", model="test")
assert quick.run("Hi").final_output == "Hello from the offline test model."
```

See [Testing your agents](testing.md) for scripted tool calls.

## Model strings

`Agent(model="provider:model")` calls `infer_model`. These prefixes are recognised:

| Prefix | Provider class | Credentials |
|---|---|---|
| `openai` | `OpenAIProvider` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `anthropic` | `AnthropicNativeProvider` (exported as `AnthropicProvider`) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| `gemini` or `google` | `GeminiNativeProvider` (exported as `GeminiProvider`) | `GEMINI_API_KEY`, or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` |
| `vertex` | `VertexAIProvider` (`pip install nexura-vertex`) | Google Application Default Credentials |
| `sarvam` | `SarvamProvider` | `SARVAM_API_KEY` |
| `ollama` | `OpenAIProvider` pointed at `http://localhost:11434/v1` | none |
| `litellm` | `LiteLLMModel` (optional extra, see below) | whatever LiteLLM needs for that provider |
| `test` | `FakeModel` | none |

Anything else raises `SDKValidationError` that lists the valid prefixes. Building a provider does not contact the network, so you can check the wiring offline by passing a placeholder key:

```python
import os

from nexura_agents import Agent, infer_model
from nexura_agents.errors import SDKValidationError

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "placeholder-not-a-real-key"
model = infer_model("openai:gpt-4o-mini")
assert type(model).__name__ == "OpenAIProvider"
assert model.model == "gpt-4o-mini"

agent = Agent(name="A", instructions="x", model="openai:gpt-4o-mini")
assert type(agent.model).__name__ == "OpenAIProvider"

try:
    infer_model("llama")  # no "provider:" prefix
except SDKValidationError as exc:
    assert "Unknown model" in str(exc)
else:
    raise AssertionError("expected SDKValidationError")
```

A string gives you the default settings of each provider. To change a timeout, a base URL or a key, build the provider yourself. All HTTP providers take `api_key`, `base_url`, `timeout` (seconds, default 30) and `transport` (an `httpx` transport, which is how the tests here stay offline).

## Live calls

These need real credentials and are billed to your account. The automated docs tests skip them.

```python notest
from nexura_agents import Agent

agent = Agent(name="Support", instructions="Be brief.", model="openai:gpt-4o-mini")
print(agent.run("Summarize our refund policy in one line.").final_output)
```

Set the key in your environment first (`export OPENAI_API_KEY=...`) or pass `api_key=` to the provider class. Do not put keys in source files.

## Provider conformance

Each adapter is checked against the providers' current API documentation by a conformance suite (`tests/providers/conformance/`). The suite replays recorded request and response fixtures (`tests/providers/fixtures/<provider>/`, each naming the documentation page it was taken from and the date it was read) through mock HTTP transports, so it runs offline and in CI without keys. For every provider it checks a plain reply, a tool-call round trip (parallel calls where the API has them), structured output, streamed text and streamed tool-call arguments, usage mapping and the budget settlement it produces, the mapping of errors to Nexura's error types, and the shape of the request Nexura sends.

| Provider (class) | Fixture-verified (2026-10-21) | Live-verified |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Chat Completions (`OpenAIProvider`) | reply, parallel tool calls, `response_format` json_schema (strict), streaming text and tool arguments, usage (cached, cache-write, reasoning tokens), auth, 429 with `Retry-After`, quota 429 (not retried), 503 overloaded, context too long, content filter, refusal | never |
| OpenAI Responses API (`OpenAIResponsesProvider`) | reply, parallel function calls with reasoning items sent back (also after streaming), `text.format` json_schema, streaming events, usage, `incomplete` (max tokens, content filter), `failed`, in-stream errors | never |
| Anthropic Messages (`AnthropicNativeProvider`) | reply, parallel `tool_use` with thinking blocks kept, `output_config.format` JSON outputs (forced-tool fallback for older models), streaming text and `input_json_delta`, cumulative `message_delta` usage, prompt-cache usage, stop reasons (`refusal`, `model_context_window_exceeded`, `pause_turn`), 401, 429 with `retry-after`, 529 and in-stream `overloaded_error`, prompt too long, 413 | never |
| Gemini API (`GeminiNativeProvider`) | reply with thought summaries hidden, parallel `functionCall` with ids and `thoughtSignature`, `systemInstruction`, `responseSchema`, streaming, `usageMetadata` (cached, thoughts, tool-use prompt), `MAX_TOKENS`, blocked prompts and `SAFETY` stops, `API_KEY_INVALID`, 429 with `RetryInfo`, per-day quota (not retried), 503, context too long | **2026-10-20** (`gemini-2.5-flash`: reply, one tool call, streaming, structured answer) |
| Vertex AI (`VertexAIProvider`, `nexura-vertex`) | the Gemini wire format on the Vertex endpoint with an OAuth token, errors | **2026-10-08** (`gemini-2.5-flash`: reply, tool call, streaming) |
| Ollama, local (`OpenAIProvider` at `localhost:11434/v1`) | reply, tool call, a tool call streamed in one chunk, usage, `max_tokens` (not `max_completion_tokens`) | never |
| Sarvam (`SarvamProvider`) | reply (reasoning text kept out of the answer), streaming with the final usage chunk, reasoning tokens, quota 429 (not retried), 403, 500 | never |
| LiteLLM (`LiteLLMModel`) | OpenAI-shaped replies with tool calls and usage through an injected `completion`, quota and content-policy errors | never (offline mock responses only) |

"Fixture-verified" means the adapter handles the documented wire format; it does not prove a live model behaves the same. Only the two live checks above have been run against real APIs.

## Live canaries (opt-in)

`scripts/live_canary.py` runs one tiny fixed scenario per provider against the real API: a plain reply, one tool call and its follow-up, a streamed reply and a structured answer, each capped at 256 output tokens. That is roughly 600 to 2,000 tokens per provider, well under one US cent at October 2026 list prices of the default small models; Ollama runs locally and costs nothing.

It sends nothing unless `NEXURA_LIVE_CANARY=1` is set and the provider's credential is present (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `SARVAM_API_KEY`; Vertex AI needs `NEXURA_CANARY_VERTEX_PROJECT` and Application Default Credentials; a local Ollama needs `NEXURA_CANARY_OLLAMA_MODEL`). CI never sets `NEXURA_LIVE_CANARY`, and a test fails if a workflow does.

```bash notest
export NEXURA_LIVE_CANARY=1 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...
uv run python scripts/live_canary.py --provider anthropic
```

Each provider that ran writes `evidence/live_canary/live_canary_<provider>_<date>.json` with the model, every check and its usage, pass or fail and the UTC time. The key is never written: the file names the variable and a masked value such as `sk-...(164 chars)`.

## OpenAI Responses API

`OpenAIResponsesProvider` talks to `POST /v1/responses`, which OpenAI recommends for new work. It takes the same arguments as `OpenAIProvider` plus `store` (default `False`). It sends the whole conversation every turn, system messages as `instructions`, tools as Responses function tools (`strict: false` unless your tool sets it) and a schema as `text.format`. Reasoning items that come back next to function calls are sent back with the tool outputs, as the API requires: from the message's `provider_data` for whole responses, and from the provider's own record of recent calls for streamed ones (so keep using the same provider object across the turns of a streamed run).

```python notest
from nexura_agents import Agent
from nexura_agents.providers.openai import OpenAIResponsesProvider

agent = Agent(name="Support", instructions="Be brief.", model=OpenAIResponsesProvider("gpt-5.4-nano"))
print(agent.run("Summarize our refund policy in one line.").final_output)
```

`OpenAIProvider` and `OpenAIChatModel` send `max_completion_tokens` to api.openai.com (reasoning models reject the deprecated `max_tokens`) and `max_tokens` to any other `base_url`, such as Ollama, vLLM or LM Studio. Set the instance attribute `max_tokens_param` to override.

## Errors you can catch

| Error (`nexura_agents.providers.errors` unless noted) | When | Retried by `RetryModel` |
|---|---|---|
| `ProviderAuthError` (`nexura_agents.errors`) | 401/403, Gemini `API_KEY_INVALID` | no |
| `ProviderRateLimitedError` | 429 throttling; `retry_after` from `Retry-After` or Gemini `RetryInfo` | yes |
| `ProviderQuotaExceededError` | 429 for an exhausted quota, credit balance or spend limit (`insufficient_quota`, Gemini per-day quotas, Sarvam `insufficient_quota_error`); still a `ProviderRateLimitError` | no |
| `ProviderServerError` | 5xx, Anthropic 529 and in-stream `overloaded_error`; `retry_after` when the server sent one | yes |
| `ProviderContextLengthError` | the prompt is longer than the context window | no (see `trim_history`) |
| `ProviderContentFilterError` | a blocked prompt, or an answer withheld with nothing returned (`reason` holds the provider's code) | no |
| `ProviderClientError` | other 4xx | no |

## Vertex AI

`VertexAIProvider` serves Gemini models from Google Cloud. It signs requests with OAuth access tokens, not API keys. By default it uses Application Default Credentials (ADC) through `google-auth`, which the `nexura-vertex` package installs:

```bash
pip install nexura-vertex
gcloud auth application-default login
gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project YOUR_PROJECT
```

```python notest
from nexura_agents import Agent
from nexura_vertex import VertexAIProvider

model = VertexAIProvider("gemini-2.5-flash", project="YOUR_PROJECT", location="global")
print(model.project, model.credential_source, model.quota_project)
agent = Agent(name="Support", instructions="Be brief.", model=model)
print(agent.run("Say hello.").final_output)
```

How the provider picks its settings:

- **Project.** The `project=` argument first, then `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, then `CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT`, then the project of your credentials. On a Google Cloud VM the credentials' project is the VM's project, which may not be the one you want to bill. If no project is found, it raises `ProviderAuthError`.
- **Location.** `location="global"` (the default) or a region such as `"asia-south1"`. A region changes the host to `asia-south1-aiplatform.googleapis.com`.
- **Quota project.** If your credentials carry a quota project (set with `set-quota-project`), it is sent as the `x-goog-user-project` header so that project is billed. It is available as `provider.quota_project`.
- **Where credentials came from.** `provider.credential_source` is a plain-text description (for example your user login or a VM service account), which helps when billing lands in the wrong project.
- **Your own tokens.** Pass `token_provider=` (a sync or async callable that returns an access token) to skip ADC. This is also how the example below runs offline.

Missing credentials, a missing `google-auth` install, a missing project, and HTTP 401 or 403 from Google all raise `ProviderAuthError`. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

The example below uses a fake token and `httpx.MockTransport`, so nothing leaves your machine. The mock also reports `thoughtsTokenCount`, which becomes `usage.reasoning_tokens`.

```python
import asyncio

import httpx

from nexura_agents import Agent, Runner
from nexura_vertex import VertexAIProvider

seen: list[httpx.Request] = []


def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
    seen.append(request)
    return httpx.Response(
        200,
        json={
            "candidates": [
                {
                    "content": {"role": "model", "parts": [{"text": "Hi from Vertex"}]},
                    "finishReason": "STOP",
                }
            ],
            "usageMetadata": {
                "promptTokenCount": 7,
                "candidatesTokenCount": 5,
                "thoughtsTokenCount": 25,
                "totalTokenCount": 37,
            },
        },
    )


provider = VertexAIProvider(
    "gemini-2.5-flash",
    project="demo-project",
    location="asia-south1",
    token_provider=lambda: "fake-token",
    transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler),
)
agent = Agent(name="V", instructions="Be brief.", model=provider)
result = asyncio.run(Runner().run_async(agent, "hello"))

assert result.final_output == "Hi from Vertex"
assert seen[0].headers["Authorization"] == "Bearer fake-token"
assert seen[0].url.host == "asia-south1-aiplatform.googleapis.com"
assert "/projects/demo-project/locations/asia-south1/" in seen[0].url.path
assert result.usage.reasoning_tokens == 25
assert result.usage.completion_tokens == 30  # 5 visible + 25 thinking
```

`examples/live/vertex_check.py` is a runnable live check for Vertex AI. It sends three short billed requests (plain text, a tool call and a streamed reply) using your ADC login and prints a JSON report. Run it yourself; tests and CI never do:

```bash
uv run python examples/live/vertex_check.py --project YOUR_PROJECT
```

For OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini (API key) and Sarvam, `examples/live/provider_check.py`
runs the same checks plus a structured (typed) answer, using the provider's key from your
environment. It refuses to start without a key:

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY=...
uv run python examples/live/provider_check.py --provider openai   # or anthropic, gemini, sarvam
```

## LiteLLM (100+ providers)

`LiteLLMModel` sends requests through [LiteLLM](https://docs.litellm.ai/), which reaches Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, Groq, Mistral, Together, OpenRouter and many more behind one interface. It is an optional extra, so the core install stays small:

```bash
pip install "nexura-agents[litellm]"
export LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True   # stop LiteLLM fetching its cost map over HTTP at import
```

Set `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` in your environment before litellm is first imported. The SDK never changes `os.environ` or LiteLLM's globals for you.

Use any LiteLLM model string, either directly or as `"litellm:<model string>"` with `infer_model` and `Agent(model=...)`:

```python notest
from nexura_agents import Agent, LiteLLMModel, RetryModel

# Credentials come from each provider's usual environment variables (AWS_*, AZURE_*, GROQ_API_KEY, ...).
bedrock = LiteLLMModel("bedrock/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0", timeout=60)
local = LiteLLMModel("ollama/llama3.1", api_base="http://localhost:11434")

agent = Agent(name="Support", instructions="Be brief.", model=RetryModel(bedrock))
# or: Agent(name="Support", instructions="Be brief.", model="litellm:groq/llama-3.1-8b-instant")
print(agent.run("Summarize our refund policy in one line.").final_output)
```

`api_key`, `api_base` and `timeout` are optional; extra keyword arguments such as `temperature` or `max_tokens` are passed to `litellm.acompletion` unchanged. Messages, tools, tool results and attachments use the OpenAI chat format, so which attachment kinds work depends on the underlying model.

Retries are owned by the SDK. Every call passes `num_retries=0` and `max_retries=0`, so LiteLLM never retries on its own; wrap the model in `RetryModel` or `FallbackModel` (see below). LiteLLM errors are mapped by HTTP status: 401/403 to `ProviderAuthError`, 429 to `ProviderRateLimitedError` (with `retry_after` when the response has a `Retry-After` header), 5xx to `ProviderServerError`, a 4xx about the context window to `ProviderContextLengthError`, other 4xx to `ProviderClientError`, and timeouts and connection failures to `ProviderRequestError`.

Both `LiteLLMModel` and `OpenAIChatModel` stream text when you ask for it: `Runner.stream_async(agent, prompt, stream_text=True)` emits real `TEXT_DELTA` events as chunks arrive, assembles tool-call arguments split across chunks, and ends with the provider's usage and finish reason. `model.generate()` is unchanged and still returns whole responses, and `stream=True` is still rejected in `LiteLLMModel(**options)`. Internally `stream()` sends `stream=True` with `stream_options={"include_usage": True}` (LiteLLM keeps `num_retries=0`). Errors, including ones raised mid-stream, map to the same typed errors as `generate()`; a stream that errors or ends early never produces a final answer (text already emitted as deltas is not committed), and closing or cancelling the run closes the HTTP stream or LiteLLM stream wrapper. Turns that send a native output schema stream too (with `PARTIAL_OUTPUT` events, see [Structured output](structured-output.md#streaming-the-output)); models without `streams_response_schema`, such as the Anthropic provider on Claude models older than 4.5, answer them in one piece.

## Temperature, max_tokens and stop sequences

`ModelSettings` sets generation parameters. Put them on the `Runner` for every agent, or
on an `Agent`; for each field the agent's value wins, and unset fields fall back to the
runner's. In a handoff team, each agent uses its own merged settings.

```python
from nexura_agents import Agent, FakeModel, ModelSettings, Runner

model = FakeModel(responses=["ok"])
agent = Agent(
    name="Writer",
    instructions="Write short poems.",
    model=model,
    model_settings=ModelSettings(temperature=0.9),
)
Runner(model_settings=ModelSettings(temperature=0.2, max_tokens=300)).run(agent, "hi")

assert model.calls[0]["model_settings"] == ModelSettings(temperature=0.9, max_tokens=300)
```

- Provider models (`"openai:..."`, `"anthropic:..."`, Gemini, Vertex AI and the others
  built by model strings) receive them in the request.
- `OpenAIChatModel` sends `temperature`, `max_tokens` and `stop`, both for normal and
  streaming calls. `LiteLLMModel` passes the same names to LiteLLM, and they override
  the options given to its constructor for that call.
- `RetryModel` and `FallbackModel` forward them to the wrapped models.
- Your own model receives them when its `generate` (or, with `stream_text=True`, its
  `stream`) accepts `model_settings=`. If it does not and a setting is set, the runner
  emits a `RuntimeWarning` instead of silently ignoring it.
- `ModelSettings` checks its values: `temperature` must be a number >= 0,
  `max_tokens` an integer >= 1, and `stop_sequences` a list of non-empty strings (a
  bare string is rejected, because it would become one stop sequence per character).
- An agent used as a tool (`agent.as_tool()`) runs on its own runner, so it does not
  inherit the outer runner's settings. Set `model_settings` on that agent, or pass
  `as_tool(runner=...)`.

## Sampling, seeds, reasoning and extra fields

`ModelSettings` also takes `top_p`, `seed`, `presence_penalty`, `frequency_penalty`,
`reasoning_effort` (`"minimal"`/`"low"`/`"medium"`/`"high"`), `thinking_budget_tokens` and
`extra` (a dict merged into the request body last, for options the SDK does not model).
They merge field by field like the others; `extra` dicts merge key by key.

```python
from nexura_agents import ModelSettings

reasoning = ModelSettings(reasoning_effort="low", seed=7)  # OpenAI reasoning models
thinking = ModelSettings(thinking_budget_tokens=2048, max_tokens=8000)  # Claude, Gemini
custom = ModelSettings(extra={"user": "customer-42"})  # any provider field
assert custom.merged(ModelSettings(extra={"metadata": {"t": 1}})).extra == {
    "user": "customer-42",
    "metadata": {"t": 1},
}
```

| Setting | OpenAI / Ollama / `OpenAIChatModel` | LiteLLM | Gemini / Vertex AI | Anthropic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `top_p` | `top_p` | `top_p` | `topP` | `top_p` |
| `seed` | `seed` | `seed` | `seed` | not supported |
| `presence_penalty`, `frequency_penalty` | same names | same names | `presencePenalty`, `frequencyPenalty` | not supported |
| `reasoning_effort` | `reasoning_effort` | `reasoning_effort` | not supported | `output_config.effort` (models with effort; `"minimal"` sent as `"low"`) |
| `thinking_budget_tokens` | not supported | `thinking` | `thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget` (0 = off) | `thinking` (see below; 0 = off) |
| `extra` | merged into the body | passed as keyword arguments | merged into the body | merged into the body |

- A setting that a provider does not support is not sent, and the runner emits a
  `RuntimeWarning` naming it, instead of dropping it silently. Sarvam supports none of
  these except `extra`.
- Values are checked when you create `ModelSettings`: `top_p` from 0 to 1, penalties from
  -2 to 2, an integer `seed`, a known `reasoning_effort`, and a budget of 0 or more.
- `extra` adds fields; it cannot replace one the SDK already sets (`model`, `messages`,
  `stream`, or a setting such as `temperature`). That raises `SDKValidationError`, so use
  the dedicated setting instead.
- The reasoning text itself is not returned or streamed: thinking blocks never become
  the answer or a `TEXT_DELTA`. Reasoning *token counts* are reported in
  `Usage.reasoning_tokens` (see below).
- **Anthropic extended thinking** follows the API's rules, which are checked before
  anything is sent:
  - The budget must be at least 1024 and below `max_tokens`.
  - `temperature` must be unset or 1.
  - `top_p` must be between 0.95 and 1.
  - It works with tools. The thinking blocks the model returns, including their
    `signature`, are kept on the assistant message (`Message.provider_data`) and sent
    back before the tool results, as Anthropic requires. Streamed thinking is assembled
    the same way. The blocks are saved in sessions and checkpoints, so treat stored
    transcripts as containing the model's reasoning. Other providers ignore them.
  - It cannot force a tool call: `tool_choice="required"` or a tool name, and native
    structured output (which forces a tool), raise `SDKValidationError`.

## Per-model headers, extra body and query parameters

`OpenAIChatModel` takes constructor-level defaults for gateways and compatible servers that need them. They apply to both `generate()` and `stream()`:

```python
import asyncio

import httpx
from nexura_agents import Message, ModelSettings
from nexura_agents.models.openai import OpenAIChatModel

seen: list[httpx.Request] = []


def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
    seen.append(request)
    return httpx.Response(
        200, json={"choices": [{"message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "ok"}}]}
    )


model = OpenAIChatModel(
    "gpt-4o-mini",
    api_key="sk-demo",
    headers={"X-Team": "support"},
    extra_body={"user": "default-user", "metadata": {"tier": "free"}},
    query_params={"api-version": "2024-06-01"},
    transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler),
)
settings = ModelSettings(extra={"user": "customer-42"})
asyncio.run(model.generate([Message(role="user", content="hi")], model_settings=settings))
assert seen[0].headers["x-team"] == "support"
assert seen[0].url.params["api-version"] == "2024-06-01"
assert b'"customer-42"' in seen[0].content  # per-call extra wins over extra_body
assert b'"tier"' in seen[0].content
```

- `headers` cannot set `Content-Type`, `Accept` or the framing headers `Content-Length`, `Host`, `Transfer-Encoding` and `Connection`, and cannot set `Authorization` when `api_key` is given. Without an `api_key` you may send your own `Authorization` header. Names must be HTTP tokens, used once regardless of letter case, and values a single line. A refused header raises `SDKValidationError` at construction.
- `extra_body` cannot contain `model`, `messages`, `tools`, `stream`, `stream_options` or `response_format`, and must be JSON-serialisable; otherwise `SDKValidationError` is raised at construction. `headers`, `extra_body` and `query_params` must be dicts, and are copied, so changing yours later does not change what is sent.
- Body precedence, highest first: fields the SDK sets, `ModelSettings` fields and per-call `ModelSettings.extra`, then constructor `extra_body`.
- Error messages name the offending keys, never header values. Header values are not logged, shown in `repr()` or added to traces; `repr()` lists header names only.
- `LiteLLMModel` already forwards extra keyword arguments to `litellm.acompletion`, so use `extra_headers={...}` and `extra_body={...}` there.

## Forcing or forbidding tool calls (tool_choice)

`ModelSettings(tool_choice=...)` controls whether the model may, must or must not call a
tool:

```python
from nexura_agents import Agent, FakeModel, ModelSettings, Runner, ToolCall, tool


@tool
def lookup_order(order_id: str) -> str:
    """Find an order."""
    return f"order {order_id}: shipped"


model = FakeModel(
    responses=[[ToolCall(id="c1", name="lookup_order", arguments={"order_id": "A7"})], "Shipped."]
)
agent = Agent(
    name="Orders",
    instructions="Answer from the order system only.",
    model=model,
    tools=[lookup_order],
    model_settings=ModelSettings(tool_choice="lookup_order"),
)
assert Runner().run(agent, "Where is A7?").output == "Shipped."
assert model.calls[0]["model_settings"].tool_choice == "lookup_order"
assert model.calls[1]["model_settings"] is None  # reset to auto after the call
```

- `"auto"` is the model's default and may call tools. `"required"` means it must call
  some tool, and `"none"` that it must not. A tool's name means it must call that tool.
- After the agent has called a tool in a turn, the runner goes back to `"auto"` so the
  model can answer. Only the active agent's own calls count: after a handoff, the new
  agent starts with its configured choice, and this survives durable recovery. A forced choice would otherwise loop until `max_turns`. Pass
  `Agent(reset_tool_choice=False)` to keep the choice for every call. A new user turn
  (the next run) starts with the configured choice again.
- `"required"` or a tool name when the agent offers no tools, or a name the agent does
  not offer on this call (see `enabled` and `prepare_tools`), raises
  `SDKValidationError`. `"none"` without tools is simply dropped.
- Mapping: OpenAI, Ollama and LiteLLM send OpenAI's `tool_choice`. Gemini and Vertex AI
  send `toolConfig.functionCallingConfig` (`AUTO`/`ANY`/`NONE`, with
  `allowedFunctionNames` for one tool). Anthropic sends `tool_choice`
  (`auto`/`any`/`none`/`tool`). Sarvam has no tool support, so it does not apply. Custom
  models get it in `model_settings`.

## Reasoning tokens

Some models spend hidden "thinking" tokens before they answer. When the provider reports them, `Usage.reasoning_tokens` holds the count. It is read from OpenAI's `reasoning_tokens` and from Gemini and Vertex AI's `thoughtsTokenCount`. These tokens are already counted in `completion_tokens` (the Gemini adapter adds `thoughtsTokenCount` to the visible output count; OpenAI's completion count includes them), so do not add the two together. If the provider does not report them, the field is `None`, not zero.

OpenAI (both APIs), Sarvam and LiteLLM also fill `reasoning_tokens` from `completion_tokens_details`/`output_tokens_details`. The Anthropic adapter does not: Anthropic reports thinking only inside `output_tokens`. `ModelSettings(reasoning_effort=...)` is sent as `reasoning_effort` (Chat Completions), `reasoning.effort` (Responses) and `output_config.effort` (Anthropic, only on the models the effort docs list: Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5+, Fable, Mythos; `"minimal"` becomes `"low"`; other models get a warning and nothing is sent); `thinking_budget_tokens` sizes Gemini thinking and Anthropic extended thinking on models before Claude 4.7.

Cache usage follows one rule for every provider: `prompt_tokens` is the whole prompt, including the tokens read from a cache (`cached_prompt_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`) and written to one (`cache_creation_input_tokens`). Anthropic reports `input_tokens` without them, so the adapter adds them back; cost settlement prices each part at its own rate.

## Retry and fallback

Two wrappers add resilience. Both wrap anything with a `generate` method, so they can be nested and passed straight to an `Agent`.

`RetryModel(model, max_attempts=3, base_delay=0.5, max_delay=8.0, retry_on=...)` retries transient failures by default: `ProviderRateLimitError`, `ProviderRequestError`, `ProviderResponseError`, `ProviderServerError` (HTTP 5xx) and `TimeoutError`. The wait before retry `n` is `base_delay * 2**(n-1)`, capped at `max_delay`, with random jitter between 50% and 100% of that value. If the raised error has a numeric `retry_after` attribute, that value (capped at `max_delay`) is used instead. The built-in providers set `retry_after` on a 429 error, in seconds, when the response has a numeric `Retry-After` header (an HTTP-date value is ignored), so that delay is honored; without the header you get the exponential delay. `ProviderAuthError` is never retried, and neither are other 4xx errors (`ProviderClientError`). Every retry repeats the request, so it also repeats the token cost.

Both wrappers also stream, passing through the capabilities of the model they wrap. `RetryModel` retries a stream only if it fails before the first delta; once text has been yielded a retry would repeat it, so a later failure is raised as is. `FallbackModel` likewise moves to the next model only before the first delta. A `FallbackModel` streams only when every model it wraps can stream.

`FallbackModel(first, second, ...)` tries each model in order and moves on after any `ProviderError` or `TimeoutError`, except `ProviderAuthError`, which is raised at once so a bad key is not hidden by switching providers. `last_used` tells you which model answered. If every model fails, it raises `ProviderError` that lists each failure. Pass `fallback_on=(...)` to change what triggers a switch.

```python
from nexura_agents import Agent, FakeModel, FallbackModel, RetryModel
from nexura_agents.errors import ProviderRateLimitError

calls = {"primary": 0}


def flaky(messages, tools):
    calls["primary"] += 1
    if calls["primary"] < 3:
        raise ProviderRateLimitError("slow down (HTTP 429)")
    return "primary answer"


def always_down(messages, tools):
    raise ProviderRateLimitError("quota exhausted")


# Retry: fails twice, succeeds on the third attempt. Tiny delays keep the example fast.
retrying = RetryModel(FakeModel(handler=flaky), max_attempts=3, base_delay=0.001, max_delay=0.01)
agent = Agent(name="R", instructions="x", model=retrying)
assert agent.run("hi").final_output == "primary answer"
assert retrying.attempts_made == 3

# Fallback: the first model is down, so the second answers.
backup = FakeModel(responses=["backup answer"])
chain = FallbackModel(
    RetryModel(FakeModel(handler=always_down), max_attempts=2, base_delay=0.001, max_delay=0.01),
    backup,
)
agent = Agent(name="F", instructions="x", model=chain)
assert agent.run("hi").final_output == "backup answer"
assert chain.last_used is backup
```

### When the prompt outgrows the context window

A provider error that says the request is longer than the model's context window (OpenAI
`context_length_exceeded`, Anthropic "prompt is too long", Gemini "exceeds the maximum number
of tokens", xAI "maximum prompt length", llama.cpp and Ollama "exceeds the available context
size", and the same phrases from LiteLLM-backed providers) is raised as
`ProviderContextLengthError`. `LiteLLMModel` also recognises LiteLLM's own
`ContextWindowExceededError` class by name, whatever its message says. Streaming calls are
classified the same way: the providers read the error body of a failed stream before classifying it. It is a subclass of `ProviderClientError`, so it is never retried
unchanged and existing handlers still catch it. The providers read the start of the error body
only to recognise this case; the body is still not included in the message.

`RetryModel(model, trim_history=N)` recovers from it. It drops the oldest whole turn and calls
the model again, up to `N` times. A turn is a user message plus everything up to the next user
message, so a tool call is never separated from its result. System messages and the latest turn
are always kept. `turns_trimmed` counts what was dropped. Trimming is off by default
(`trim_history=0`), because dropping history changes what the model sees. Trimming applies when
the wrapper is called with a plain message list, which is how agents call it, for `generate()`
and for `stream()` alike. A stream trims and restarts only before its first delta; an overflow
raised after text was yielded is raised unchanged. In `FallbackModel(RetryModel(a, trim_history=N), b)`
the primary trims first and `b` is used only if trimming cannot fix it.

```python
from nexura_agents import Agent, FakeModel, Message, RetryModel
from nexura_agents.providers.errors import ProviderContextLengthError


def small_window(messages, tools):
    if sum(1 for m in messages if m.role == "user") > 2:
        raise ProviderContextLengthError("prompt is too long")
    return f"answered with {len(messages)} messages"


model = RetryModel(FakeModel(handler=small_window), trim_history=3)
history = []
for i in range(4):
    history += [Message(role="user", content=f"q{i}"), Message(role="assistant", content=f"a{i}")]
agent = Agent(name="T", instructions="x", model=model)
print(agent.run("latest", history=history).final_output)
assert model.turns_trimmed >= 1
```

## Rate limits and concurrency

`RateLimiter` is a client-side cap on model calls that you can share. `RateLimitedModel(model, limiter)` wraps a model so every `generate` and `stream` call goes through the limiter. Give the same limiter to several wrappers or agents and they are limited together, including runs started from different threads or by the sync `Agent.run`.

`RateLimiter(max_concurrent=None, requests_per_minute=None, tokens_per_minute=None)` takes any combination of three limits. All must be integers of at least 1 or `None` (no limit), otherwise it raises `SDKValidationError`.

- `max_concurrent`: at most this many calls at once. A stream counts as one call until it finishes, fails, is closed or is cancelled.
- `requests_per_minute`: at most this many calls start in any 60 second window. A burst up to the limit starts at once.
- `tokens_per_minute`: once the tokens reported in the last 60 seconds reach this number, new calls wait until older usage ages out. This is approximate. A call's tokens are only known after it finishes, so calls already running can push you past the budget, and a call whose provider reports no usage counts as 0.

Waiting uses no polling loop and respects `asyncio` cancellation: a call cancelled while it waits takes no slot and releases none. Put the limiter inside the retry wrapper, `RetryModel(RateLimitedModel(model, limiter))`, so each retry waits for its own slot. For tests, pass `clock=` (seconds, default `time.monotonic`) and `sleep=` (an awaitable, default `asyncio.sleep`).

```python
import asyncio

from nexura_agents import Agent, FakeModel, RetryModel
from nexura_agents import RateLimitedModel, RateLimiter

limiter = RateLimiter(max_concurrent=2)  # shared by every run below
model = RateLimitedModel(FakeModel(responses=["ok"], repeat_last=True), limiter)
agent = Agent(name="L", instructions="x", model=RetryModel(model))


async def main():
    results = await asyncio.gather(*(agent.run_async("hi") for _ in range(6)))
    assert all(r.final_output == "ok" for r in results)
    assert limiter.in_flight == 0


asyncio.run(main())
```

A common production chain wraps each live provider in its own `RetryModel` and joins them with `FallbackModel`:

```python notest
from nexura_agents import Agent, FallbackModel, RetryModel, infer_model

model = FallbackModel(
    RetryModel(infer_model("vertex:gemini-2.5-flash")),
    RetryModel(infer_model("anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5")),
)
agent = Agent(name="Support", instructions="Be brief.", model=model)
```

Use the model IDs your account has access to; the ones above are examples.

## Using a real model: Google Vertex AI

`VertexAIProvider` runs Gemini models on Vertex AI using your Google Cloud login, so no
API key is stored anywhere. It is the separate `nexura-vertex` package
([packages/nexura-vertex](../packages/nexura-vertex/README.md)). Any provider adapter can be an
agent's model.

```bash
pip install nexura-vertex
gcloud auth application-default login     # once per machine
gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT     # or pass project=...
```

```python notest
from nexura_vertex import VertexAIProvider

from nexura_runtime import Agent, Runner

model = VertexAIProvider("gemini-2.5-flash", location="global")  # project from gcloud
agent = Agent(name="Support", instructions="Be brief.", model=model)
print(Runner().run(agent, "Summarize our refund policy in one line.").final_output)
```

Live calls are billed to your Google Cloud project. The automated tests verify the
Vertex wire format offline with mock HTTP; they never call Google. The one live check
that has been run (by the owner, 2026-10-08) is listed in the [verification record](testing.md#verification-record).

Other providers work the same way as `Agent(model="openai:gpt-4.1-mini")` and similar
strings; `nexura-agents[litellm]` adds `"litellm:<provider>/<model>"` for others.

## Models

| String | Provider | Credentials |
|---|---|---|
| `"vertex:gemini-2.5-flash"` | Google Vertex AI | `gcloud auth application-default login` (`pip install nexura-vertex`) |
| `"gemini:gemini-2.5-flash"` | Gemini API | `GEMINI_API_KEY` |
| `"openai:gpt-4.1-mini"` | OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible server | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `"anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5"` | Anthropic (the default model of `AnthropicNativeProvider`) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| `"sarvam:sarvam-105b"` | Sarvam AI (Indian languages; the default model) | `SARVAM_API_KEY` |
| `"ollama:llama3.1"` | Local Ollama | none |
| `"test"` | Offline fake | none |
| `"litellm:bedrock/..."` | Any provider LiteLLM supports | that provider's own (`[litellm]` extra) |

Or construct a provider directly (`from nexura_vertex import VertexAIProvider`;
`VertexAIProvider(project=..., location="asia-south1")`)
for full control. Anything with an async `generate()` method works as a model.

`LiteLLMModel` supports tool calls, attachments and usage, and leaves retries to
`RetryModel` and `FallbackModel`. It streams text and typed output, and it has only been checked
offline against LiteLLM's mock responses (`examples/live/litellm_offline_check.py`), not
against live providers.

## Package overview

**Google Vertex AI (Gemini) for Nexura agents, authenticated with your Google Cloud login.**

```bash
pip install nexura-vertex   # installs nexura-agents and google-auth too
gcloud auth application-default login
```

```python notest
from nexura_agents import Agent, Runner

agent = Agent(name="Support", instructions="Answer briefly.", model="vertex:gemini-2.5-flash")
print(Runner().run(agent, "What is a refund window?").final_output)
```

- **`"vertex:<model>"` model strings.** Once this package is installed, `Agent(model=...)` and
  `nexura_agents.infer_model` build a `VertexAIProvider` from them. Without it they fail with
  "'vertex:' models are provided by the 'nexura-vertex' package, which is not installed.
  Install it with: pip install nexura-vertex".
- **Application Default Credentials.** `gcloud auth application-default login`, a
  service-account key in `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, or the metadata server of a Google
  Cloud VM. The project comes from the credentials, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, or `project=`.
  Pass `token_provider=` to supply access tokens yourself.
- **Same wire format as Gemini.** `VertexAIProvider` reuses the Gemini adapter (tools,
  streaming, structured output, multimodal parts, `gs://` file URLs) and changes only the
  endpoint, the OAuth bearer token and embeddings (`:predict`).
- Depends on `nexura-agents` only, not on `nexura-runtime`; Python 3.11 to 3.13.

> Status: **alpha** (0.4). Gemini 2.5 Flash on Vertex AI passed one live check run by the
> repository owner on 2026-10-08 (a plain reply, a tool call and streaming). Everything else is
> tested offline with mock HTTP.

## Offline example

A mock HTTP transport and a fixed token stand in for Google, so this runs without credentials.

```python
import httpx
from nexura_agents import Agent, Runner

from nexura_vertex import VertexAIProvider


def fake_vertex(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
    assert request.headers["Authorization"] == "Bearer test-token"
    assert "/projects/demo/locations/global/" in request.url.path
    return httpx.Response(
        200,
        json={
            "candidates": [
                {"content": {"role": "model", "parts": [{"text": "Hello"}]}, "finishReason": "STOP"}
            ],
            "usageMetadata": {"promptTokenCount": 3, "candidatesTokenCount": 1},
        },
    )


model = VertexAIProvider(
    "gemini-2.5-flash",
    project="demo",
    token_provider=lambda: "test-token",
    transport=httpx.MockTransport(fake_vertex),
)
result = Runner().run(Agent(name="Hi", instructions="Greet.", model=model), "hi")
print(result.final_output)
```
